rows.note: Use this for scrambling eggs into a loose cooked mass; it is the usual Cantonese cooking verb.

example.english: I scramble eggs for the children every morning.
example.traditional: 我朝朝都炒蛋畀啲細路食。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 ziu1 dou1 caau2 daan2 bei2 di1 sai3 lou6 sik6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a hurried or chaotic scramble, such as a last-minute rush.

example.english: Getting ready for work in the morning turned into a scramble at home.
example.traditional: 朝早趕返工，成個屋企搞到一陣忙亂。
example.jyutping: ziu1 zou2 gon2 faan1 gung1 sing4 go3 uk1 kei2 gaau2 dou3 jat1 zan6 mong4 lyun6

rows.note: Use this when the scramble is a final push toward a finish or goal.

example.english: With one day left before the deadline, we made a final scramble to finish the report.
example.traditional: 截稿前一日，我哋來個最後衝刺，趕住完成份報告。
example.jyutping: zit6 gou2 cin4 jat1 jat6 ngo5 dei6 lai4 go3 zeoi3 hau6 cung1 ci3 gon2 zyu6 jyun4 sing4 fan6 bou3 gou3

rows.note: Use this when someone hurries to a place by crawling or clambering with their limbs, rather than simply walking quickly.

example.english: The cat had to scramble up to the windowsill when it saw the dog.
example.traditional: 隻貓見到狗，就急急腳咁爬上窗台。
example.jyutping: zek3 maau1 gin3 dou2 gau2 zau6 gap1 gap1 goek3 gam3 paa4 soeng5 coeng1 toi1

rows.note: Use this for a period of frantic activity in which people are competing to obtain or achieve something.

example.english: There was a scramble for the limited-edition trainers as soon as they went on sale.
example.traditional: 限量波鞋一開售，網上即刻出現一輪爭奪。
example.jyutping: haan6 loeng6 bo1 haai4 jat1 hoi1 sau6 mong5 soeng6 zik1 hak1 ceot1 jin6 jat1 leon4 zang1 dyut6
